citation: 'Private Residences of Chicago.' Plate in The New Chicago Album (Chicago: Wittemann Bros., 1883): eleven engraved vignettes, among them 'Thomas Dent' (the second vignette of the middle row, left of C. P. Libby's). Newberry Library.
author: Wittemann Bros. (publisher); engraver not named
describes_date: 1883 or a little before: the house two years after its building (1881)
repository: Newberry Library (via CARLI Digital Collections, nby_chicago)
locator: The 'Thomas Dent' vignette, x 545-935 and y 465-890 px of the Prairie library's copy a19-nby-newchicagoalbum-1883-residences (2400 x 1480 px, sha256 7ba41d629fb60890a887eee4a18a0574e98aa9e9326031035ea53c809b9bc1f0): the house from the north-west. The 'B. F. Moulton' vignette (1912 Prairie), the bottom vignette of the middle column: x 940-1465 and y 790-1310 px of the same copy (T-3278).

note: A small engraved vignette of the Dent house from the north-west, the same view as the Chicagology engraving and dated, which that one is not. It draws the same house: a light, smooth street front of stone beside a brick north flank, two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard; at the front's south end a pavilion flush with the south wall and standing forward of the front, one window to a storey, carried up into an attic under a pedimented gable with paired lights and a finial in front of a steep roof; the door north of it up a stoop that climbs from the north, with an arched opening under the landing; a group of three windows to a storey north of the door; a pedimented dormer in the mansard over that group and a small one over the door; four window columns on the north flank and a hooded window on it, three dormers in its mansard, the mansard ending short of the flank's rear corner over a lower rear part; tall stacks on the north wall, one at the flank's rear corner and one at the pavilion's back.
